name: Nathan Coffee
headline: Software Engineer · C# / .NET
summary: I'm a backend developer working in C#, ASP.NET Core and SQL Server. I graduated from the University of Louisville in May 2026 after interning at Rawlings, where I built features for a healthcare claims recovery platform.
about: At Rawlings, a Machinify company, I worked in a large enterprise .NET codebase from August 2024 through December 2025. I took features through the whole cycle: work items and sprint planning in Azure DevOps, the code and its unit and integration tests, review with senior developers, and release through CI/CD pipelines.

My senior capstone went the other direction, down to the hardware. Our team built a LoRa sensor network for monitoring industrial refrigeration equipment: ESP32 nodes reading temperature and current sensors, and a Raspberry Pi gateway feeding InfluxDB and Grafana.
On my own time I build tools for the game The Bazaar: a battle simulator that runs thousands of seeded fights, and an AI assistant that reads the board and looks up item data to make recommendations.

experience.summary: Backend development on a healthcare claims recovery and payment integrity platform.
highlights: Developed and maintained backend features in C#, .NET and ASP.NET Core in an established enterprise codebase, using dependency injection, LINQ and Entity Framework Core.
Wrote and optimized SQL Server queries, stored procedures and data models for claims processing, subrogation and overpayment recovery over large volumes of healthcare data.
Built and maintained RESTful APIs and backend services behind internal tools and client-facing claims recovery applications.
Wrote unit and integration tests, and tracked down bugs and data discrepancies in claims workflows to make automated recovery and reporting more reliable.
Worked across the full SDLC in Azure DevOps (sprint planning, Git, code review, CI/CD pipelines) with senior developers, QA and product in an Agile/Scrum team.

projects.title: Bazaar Battle Sim
projects.summary: A Windows desktop app that simulates fights between two boards in The Bazaar. It runs thousands of seeded fights and reports win rates, output per item, and a health chart and combat log for a sample fight.
highlights: Combat engine in a UI-free .NET 8 class library that models cooldowns, Haste, Slow and Freeze, multicast, crits, ammo, and chains of triggers with a loop guard.
WPF front end built with MVVM. Items are imported by pasting text from BazaarDB; the parser turns it into effects and triggers and warns about anything it can't model.
Seeded runs replay exactly the same fights after one item changes. xUnit tests cover the engine and the importer.
Shares a JSON build format with a dependency-free JavaScript version that runs in the browser.

projects.title: LoRa Wireless Sensor Network
projects.summary: A multi-node wireless telemetry system for monitoring simulated industrial refrigeration equipment, built as a team with input from an industry partner.
highlights: Programmed ESP32 (Heltec LoRa32) sensor nodes in C++ to read thermocouple, BME280 environmental and current sensors over I2C and transmit the readings over LoRa at 915 MHz.
Built a Raspberry Pi gateway in Python that received packets over SPI and stored time-series data in InfluxDB, with Grafana dashboards for live monitoring.
Diagnosed a UART/SPI radio incompatibility between the gateway and the nodes, and redesigned the gateway hardware to restore communication.

projects.title: RAG-Based AI Assistant
projects.summary: An AI assistant for The Bazaar that reads the in-game board and retrieves public item data from a vector database (retrieval-augmented generation) to give context-aware recommendations.

education.school: University of Louisville, J.B. Speed School of Engineering
